contracts.contract_plain_english: For Householder QR of an m-by-n real matrix, under the paper's probabilistic rounding model and its strengthened probability-1 local-application assumption, the computed R_hat is the exact R factor of A + Delta A for some orthogonal Q, and the Frobenius backward error is bounded by c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||A||_F plus an unspecified second-order remainder; the bound inherits the all-column probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4 and (4.16)-(4.17); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).

source_evidence.observation: The paper defines the vector 2-norm, its subordinate matrix norm, the Frobenius norm ||A||_F = trace(A^T A)^(1/2), column notation a_j, modest integer constants c_i, and gamma_tilde_k(lambda) = exp((lambda sqrt(k) u + k u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 = lambda sqrt(k) u + O(u^2), with lambda > 0.
Generated rounding errors satisfy the standard relative-error model and are mean-independent random variables of mean zero.
A computed sequence of Householder applications is represented by local perturbations Delta P_j, with ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda).

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2 and Lemma 4.2 hypothesis
source_evidence.observation: The remaining section results, including Theorem 4.4, strengthen the local bound (4.2) to an assumption that it holds with probability 1 for every j.

For the computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor R_hat, there exists an orthogonal Q such that A + Delta A = Q R_hat, and all columns satisfy ||Delta a_j||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda) ||a_j||_2 + O(u^2), j=1:n, with probability at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2).

source_evidence.anchor: equations (4.18)-(4.20) and the implication sentence preceding (4.20)
source_evidence.observation: After discussing the first-order restriction m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1, the paper states that the columnwise bound (4.17) implies ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda) ||A||_F + O(u^2).

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract concerns the normwise backward error of the computed upper-trapezoidal R factor produced by Householder QR; it is specialized from applying n Householder transformations and includes the treatment of explicitly zeroed entries and computed Householder vectors described in the proof of Theorem 4.4 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4 and its proof).
binders: Matrix dimensions m,n with m >= n; input A in R^(m x n); computed upper-trapezoidal Householder QR factor R_hat in R^(m x n) (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, text following (4.19)).

Parameter lambda > 0, unit roundoff u, existential orthogonal Q in R^(m x m), perturbation Delta A with columns Delta a_j, and indices j=1,...,n (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.6); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.16)-(4.17)).
conclusions: There exists an orthogonal Q such that A + Delta A = Q R_hat (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.16)).
The normwise backward error satisfies ||Delta A||_F <= c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda) ||A||_F + O(u^2) (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).

Inherited-event conclusion: because (4.20) is obtained from the simultaneously valid columnwise bounds (4.17), it holds on that same event, whose stated probability is at least p_4(lambda,m,n) = 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2); equation (4.20) does not repeat this probability (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, implication sentence before (4.20)).
constants_and_indexing: The leading factor is exactly c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda): the square-root factor is indexed by n, while gamma_tilde is indexed by m (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).
The source columnwise estimate applies simultaneously for j=1:n and has probability lower bound 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17)).
The same lambda occurs both outside gamma_tilde_m(lambda) and inside its definition (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.6); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).
definitions_and_conventions: ||A||_F = trace(A^T A)^(1/2), and a_j denotes column j of A (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm-convention paragraph).
gamma_tilde_m(lambda) = exp((lambda sqrt(m) u + m u^2)/(1-u)) - 1 = lambda sqrt(m)u + O(u^2), with lambda > 0 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.6), specialized from index n to m).
The c_i, including c_6, are integer constants of modest size rather than dimension-dependent quantities (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm-convention paragraph).
Delta A is a backward perturbation of the input because it appears in the exact relation A + Delta A = Q R_hat with Q orthogonal (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.16)).
error_notions: Delta A is a normwise input backward error for the computed R_hat, certified through an exact QR relation with an orthogonal Q (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.16)).
Equation (4.20) is the Frobenius aggregation of the columnwise 2-norm backward errors in (4.17) (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, sentence before (4.20)).
exceptional_values: No separate NaN, infinity, overflow, or underflow clauses are stated; applicability is conditional on elementary operations satisfying the relative-error model (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.4)).

Only lambda > 0 is stated for gamma_tilde; no additional restriction is imposed to make 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2) nonnegative, so for small lambda that probability lower bound can be vacuous (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.6); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17)).
higher_order_terms: The displayed bound retains an additive O(u^2) term and is explicitly described as a first-order backward-error result (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, paragraph following Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).

For r=n, the paper estimates the omitted second-order contribution at scale n^2 gamma_tilde_m(lambda)^2 ||b||_2, approximately n^2 m u^2 ||b||_2 when constants and lambda are omitted (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, higher-order discussion continuing onto PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155).
The condition m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 is used to ensure the omitted higher-order terms do not overturn the claimed sqrt(mn)u growth (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.18) and subsequent ratio argument).
hypotheses: R_hat is obtained from A by the Householder QR algorithm (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4).
The rounding errors obey Model 1.5: the standard relative-error model with errors generated in computation order, mean independent, and of mean zero (PDF p. 3, printed p. 1148, Model 1.5).

The local application-error bound ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) is assumed to hold with probability 1 for every Householder application (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2 hypothesis).

For the paper's interpretation that the first-order error grows like sqrt(mn)u rather than being dominated by omitted terms, it imposes m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.18) and following discussion).
implicit_context: Theorem 4.4 inherits the standing QR dimension condition m >= n even though that inequality is not repeated in its opening sentence (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, discussion following (4.19)).

Q is an exact existential orthogonal factor, while R_hat is the computed factor; (4.20) is not a forward-error comparison with a separately specified exact R (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4 and (4.16)).

The Frobenius estimate is obtained by aggregating the all-column event in (4.17), not by applying a new probabilistic argument at (4.20) (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Lemma 4.3 proof and (4.17); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, implication sentence before (4.20)).
norms: The conclusion uses the Frobenius norm on both Delta A and A (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).

Its source bounds use the Euclidean 2-norm on each column (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17)); the paper defines the vector 2-norm and corresponding subordinate matrix norm globally (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm-convention paragraph).
numerical_model: Elementary operations satisfy fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.4)).
Model 1.5 additionally requires computation-order mean independence and zero mean (PDF p. 3, printed p. 1148, Model 1.5).

The analysis assumes the local bound (4.2) with probability 1, although its preceding derivation only supplies probability at least 1 - 2rm exp(-lambda^2/2) (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.5)-(4.6) and paragraph before Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, discussion before (4.20)).

undebatable_constraints: The bound is Frobenius-to-Frobenius and concerns the same Delta A appearing in A + Delta A = Q R_hat (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.16); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).
The exact leading expression is c_6 lambda sqrt(n) gamma_tilde_m(lambda); neither the sqrt(n) factor nor the m index on gamma_tilde may be changed (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20)).

The additive O(u^2) term is part of the displayed claim and cannot be silently deleted or converted into an exact all-orders inequality (PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, (4.20) and preceding higher-order discussion).
The result is conditional on Model 1.5 and the probability-1 version of the local perturbation bound (4.2) (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, Theorem 4.4).

The probability attached to the source columnwise event is at least 1 - 2mn exp(-lambda^2), and the Frobenius implication does not introduce a different probability (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, (4.17); PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, implication before (4.20)).

contracts.contract_plain_english: For a rectangular real matrix B, form the symmetric block matrix with B and B^T in the off-diagonal blocks and zeros on the diagonal. Its largest eigenvalue is exactly the operator 2-norm of B; this is a deterministic identity used to transfer a symmetric matrix concentration theorem to rectangular matrices (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)-(3.4) and following paragraph).

source_evidence.observation: The paper uses the vector 2-norm and corresponding subordinate matrix norm.
Within section 3, lambda_max denotes the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix.
For a rectangular matrix B, the paper defines its symmetric dilation phi(B) as the block matrix [[0,B],[B^T,0]] and states lambda_max(phi(B)) = ||B||_2.
The identity is used to pass from the symmetric matrix concentration theorem to a theorem for nonsymmetric d_1-by-d_2 matrices.

statement.algorithm_linkage: There is no numerical algorithm in the claim itself; the paper uses the symmetric dilation and identity (3.4) to derive the nonsymmetric matrix concentration inequality in Theorem 3.2 from Theorem 3.1 (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, paragraph following (3.4)).
binders: A rectangular matrix B; if its dimensions are denoted d_1 by d_2 as in the immediately following theorem, the block layout makes phi(B) a (d_1+d_2)-by-(d_1+d_2) matrix (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3) and Theorem 3.2).
constants_and_indexing: The two diagonal zero blocks have sizes d_1-by-d_1 and d_2-by-d_2, while B and B^T occupy the d_1-by-d_2 and d_2-by-d_1 off-diagonal blocks; these sizes are forced by (3.3) and the d_1-by-d_2 notation immediately following it (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3) and Theorem 3.2).
No numerical constants or index offsets occur in (3.3)-(3.4) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)-(3.4)).
definitions_and_conventions: phi(B) is called the symmetric dilation of B (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, sentence containing (3.3)).
lambda_max is the largest algebraic eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, section 3 notation paragraph).

||B||_2 is the subordinate matrix 2-norm, equivalently the largest singular value in this rectangular-matrix setting (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm-convention paragraph; PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.4)).
The off-diagonal lower-left block is B^T, so the displayed dilation is symmetric in the paper's real-matrix setting (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)).
exceptional_values: No nonzero or nonsingularity condition is imposed on B, and no exceptional-value cases are identified for (3.3)-(3.4) (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, text and equations (3.3)-(3.4)).
hypotheses: B is rectangular; equations (3.3)-(3.4) state no rank, invertibility, nonzero, probabilistic, or floating-point hypothesis (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, text immediately before (3.3) and equations (3.3)-(3.4)).
implicit_context: The paper works with real matrices and uses transpose T; the field is not restated locally at (3.3) (PDF p. 1, printed p. 1146, introductory QR setting; PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)).
The named dimensions d_1,d_2 occur in Theorem 3.2 immediately after the definition rather than in equation (3.3) itself (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, paragraph after (3.4) and Theorem 3.2).

The identity is exact and deterministic; it is a linear-algebra input to the subsequent probabilistic concentration result, not itself a probability statement (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)-(3.5)).
norms: The right side is the subordinate operator 2-norm of the rectangular matrix B (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm-convention paragraph; PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.4)).
The left side is lambda_max, not the spectral radius or a norm of phi(B), although for this dilation its value equals ||B||_2 (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, section notation and (3.4)).

undebatable_constraints: The block order is exactly top-right B and bottom-left B^T, with zero diagonal blocks (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)).
The claimed scalar is the largest eigenvalue lambda_max(phi(B)), not the maximum absolute eigenvalue written as a separate operation (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, section notation and (3.4)).
The right side is ||B||_2, the subordinate matrix 2-norm (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, norm convention; PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.4)).
The claim is an exact deterministic identity for a rectangular matrix and carries no rounding model, probability, error term, or big-O remainder (PDF p. 5, printed p. 1150, (3.3)-(3.4)).

contracts.contract_plain_english: Expanding the computed product of r perturbed Householder applications and retaining first-order terms gives the exact transformed vector plus one term for each possible insertion of Delta P_j, with all multiple-perturbation terms left as O(u^2). Factoring out Q^T rewrites those insertions using F_j=P_1...P_j Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1, which prepares the matrices for the subsequent concentration argument (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)-(4.9) and following sentence).

source_evidence.observation: The computation-order rounding errors satisfy the standard relative-error model and are mean-independent random variables of mean zero.

The paper takes given exact Householder matrices P_i = I - v_i v_i^T in R^(m x m), with v_i^T v_i = 2, defines b_(r+1) = P_r...P_1 b, and represents the computed result as (P_r+Delta P_r)...(P_1+Delta P_1)b.

Assuming the local bound (4.2) with probability 1, the proof expands the perturbed product to first order as b_hat_(r+1) = b_(r+1) + (sum from j=1 to r of P_r...P_(j+1) Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1 + O(u^2))b = b_(r+1) + Q^T(sum from j=1 to r of F_j + O(u^2))b, where F_j = P_1...P_j Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1.
The proof introduces F_j so that it can seek E(F_j | F_(j-1),...,F_1)=0 and apply Theorem 3.2 with X_k=F_k.
When r=n, the paper says the O(u^2) part dropped from the expansion contains binomial(n,2) second-order terms.

source_evidence.anchor: continuation of higher-order discussion and equation (4.18)
source_evidence.observation: Omitting constants and lambda, the second-order contribution is bounded at scale n^2 gamma_tilde_m(lambda)^2 ||b||_2, approximately n^2 m u^2 ||b||_2, and m^(1/2)n^(3/2)u < 1 is used for first-order dominance.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The equations describe the sequential floating-point application of r given Householder transformations to one vector, before the paper applies the result columnwise to a matrix or specializes it to Householder QR (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, opening of section 4 and Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2 proof).
binders: Positive matrix dimension m and number of transformations r; indices i,j=1,...,r; starting vector b=b_1 in R^m (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1).
Given exact vectors v_i in R^m and Householder matrices P_i = I - v_i v_i^T in R^(m x m), normalized by v_i^T v_i=2 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1).

Local perturbation matrices Delta P_j in R^(m x m), exact product result b_(r+1), computed result b_hat_(r+1), matrices F_j, and Q=(P_r...P_2P_1)^T (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.1); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2 and (4.8)-(4.9)).
conclusions: b_hat_(r+1) = b_(r+1) + (sum_(j=1)^r P_r...P_(j+1) Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1 + O(u^2))b (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, first line of (4.8)).
Equivalently, b_hat_(r+1) = b_(r+1) + Q^T(sum_(j=1)^r F_j + O(u^2))b (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, second line of (4.8)).
For each j=1:r, F_j = P_1...P_j Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.9)).
constants_and_indexing: The summation range is exactly j=1:r (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)).
The single-insertion term before factoring is P_r...P_(j+1) Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1; there is no P_j adjacent to Delta P_j in that unfactored term (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, first line of (4.8)).
After factoring Q^T, F_j has the exact order P_1...P_j Delta P_j P_(j-1)...P_1; the left product includes P_j and the right product begins at P_(j-1) (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.9)).

The local perturbation bound uses c_5 and gamma_tilde indexed by m, while the final enclosing lemma uses c_6 lambda sqrt(r) gamma_tilde_m(lambda) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.7)).
definitions_and_conventions: b_(r+1)=P_r...P_1b is the exact transformed vector, whereas b_hat_(r+1) is the computed vector represented by the perturbed product (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1 and (4.1)).
Q=(P_r...P_1)^T, hence Q^T=P_r...P_1 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2).

Delta P_j is the local matrix perturbation induced by the computed application of P_j; the paper bounds its subordinate 2-norm but does not define it as a Householder matrix (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.1)-(4.4)).
F_j is the transformed single-perturbation insertion used as X_j in the later matrix-concentration argument (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.9) and following sentence).
error_notions: Equation (4.8) is a first-order forward expansion of b_hat_(r+1)-b_(r+1) into single local perturbation insertions; it is not itself the final backward-error statement (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)-(4.9) and Lemma 4.2).
The enclosing lemma subsequently interprets the accumulated matrix sum as a perturbation Delta b of the original vector before exact multiplication by Q^T (PDF p. 8, printed p. 1153, (4.14)).
exceptional_values: The given Householder vectors satisfy v_i^T v_i=2, so zero vectors are excluded by normalization (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1).

No separate overflow, underflow, NaN, or infinity conditions are stated in Lemma 4.2; the calculation is conditional on the standard relative-error model and the assumed local bound (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.4); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2).
higher_order_terms: Both forms of (4.8) explicitly retain an O(u^2) matrix remainder inside the parentheses that multiply b (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)).

For r=n, the later discussion identifies binomial(n,2) second-order terms and bounds their aggregate, omitting constants and lambda, by a quantity of scale n^2 gamma_tilde_m(lambda)^2||b||_2, approximately n^2 m u^2||b||_2 (PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, higher-order discussion; PDF p. 10, printed p. 1155, continuation before (4.18)).
The paper does not replace O(u^2) in (4.8) by an explicit remainder matrix or an exact finite sum there (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)).
hypotheses: The exact recurrence is b_(j+1)=P_j b_j=b_j-(v_j^T b_j)v_j for j=1:r, with b_(r+1)=P_r...P_1b (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1).
The computed result has the perturbed-product representation b_hat_(r+1)=(P_r+Delta P_r)...(P_1+Delta P_1)b (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.1)).
The computation is under Model 1.5 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 3, printed p. 1148, Model 1.5).
Lemma 4.2 assumes ||Delta P_j||_2 <= c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda) with probability 1 for every j (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2 hypothesis).
implicit_context: The first equality in (4.8) is obtained by retaining terms containing exactly one Delta P_j from the product (4.1); products containing at least two perturbations are absorbed into O(u^2) (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.1); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8); PDF p. 9, printed p. 1154, later higher-order discussion).

The enclosing Lemma 4.2 later converts this forward expansion into b_hat_(r+1)=Q^T(b+Delta b) with ||Delta b||_2 <= c_6 lambda sqrt(r) gamma_tilde_m(lambda)||b||_2+O(u^2), with probability at least 1-2m exp(-lambda^2) (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.7); PDF p. 8, printed p. 1153, (4.12)-(4.14)).
norms: No norm occurs in equations (4.8)-(4.9) themselves; their standing local hypothesis uses the subordinate matrix 2-norm ||Delta P_j||_2 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)-(4.9)).
The enclosing Lemma 4.2 measures the resulting backward vector perturbation in the Euclidean 2-norm relative to ||b||_2 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.7)).
numerical_model: Elementary operations obey fl(x op y)=(x op y)(1+delta), |delta|<=u, and Model 1.5 makes the generated errors mean independent and zero mean (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.4); PDF p. 3, printed p. 1148, Model 1.5).

The first-order expansion uses Delta P_j=O(u) through the assumed norm bound ||Delta P_j||_2<=c_5 gamma_tilde_m(lambda), with gamma_tilde_m(lambda)=O(u) for fixed m and lambda (PDF p. 2, printed p. 1147, (1.6); PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, (4.2)).

The probability-1 local-bound assumption is stronger than Lemma 4.1's derived high-probability bound and is explicitly adopted for Lemma 4.2 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, paragraph preceding Lemma 4.2).

undebatable_constraints: The exact and computed quantities must remain distinct: b_(r+1)=P_r...P_1b is exact, while b_hat_(r+1) comes from the perturbed product (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1 and (4.1)).
Every first-order summand contains exactly one Delta P_j in the product order shown in (4.8) (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)).
F_j must be defined with left factor P_1...P_j and right factor P_(j-1)...P_1; changing either endpoint changes the sourced identity (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.9)).
The O(u^2) remainder is part of both displayed forms of the expansion and cannot be silently discarded (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, (4.8)).

The P_i are given exact normalized Householder matrices in this lemma-level setup; Delta P_j are general local perturbation matrices and are not asserted to be symmetric, orthogonal, or Householder (PDF p. 6, printed p. 1151, Lemma 4.1 and (4.1)-(4.4)).
The probability-1 form of the local norm bound (4.2) is an explicit assumption of the enclosing Lemma 4.2 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 1152, Lemma 4.2 hypothesis).
